header.running_head: The fervour that Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA) had to Spend in the Path of Allaah

When Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) refused to submit to his request, Hadhrat Umar (RA) himself went to Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) and informed him of his intentions. Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) responded by saying, "Since Rasulullaah ﷺ had sent me so that I may recover my losses, I do not have to do this." (Since Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) had paid back the capital he took from the Zakaah funds, he felt entitled to the profits he earned. Hadhrat Umar (RA) was of the opinion that although Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) could use what he needed, the excess was to be returned to the public whose money was a means to the profits). When Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) met Hadhrat Umar (RA) some time later, he said, "I have obeyed you and have done as you instructed me. I saw in a dream that I was surrounded by water and was in danger of drowning when you rescued me, O Umar." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) then went to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) and related the incident to him. He (disclosed all his assets and) swore that he would not hide anything, even disclosing the whip that he owned. Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) said, "By Allaah! I shall take none of this from you. You may have it all as a gift." Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Now this is good for you and permissible." Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) thereafter left for Shaam.[^1]

Another narration from the son of Hadhrat Ka'b bin Maalik (RA) states that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was an extremely youthful, handsome and generous man who was amongst the most righteous persons of his tribe. He gave away everything that he was asked for until all his wealth was tied up in debt. The rest of the narration is as quoted above.[^2]
The Narration of Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) Concerning the Generosity of Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA)

Hadhrat Jabbir (RA) reports that Hadhrat Mu'aadh bin Jabal (RA) was amongst the most handsome of people, amongst those with the best character and the most open-handed. However, (to assist others) he accumulated a large debt and when his creditors started pushing him to pay, he hid away from them in his house for several days. The creditors eventually sought Rasulullaah ﷺ's assistance. When Rasulullaah ﷺ sent for Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), he came with the creditors in trail. They pleaded, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Please claim our dues from him." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Allah will shower His mercy on the person who is charitable towards him (who writes off the debt)." Consequently, some of them wrote off their debts while others refused. They still insisted, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Do reclaim our rights from him." Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "O Mu'aadh!
